text:
maria: Quick sync — RFC follow-up: proposal to converge Python/TS/Go SDKs around a single resumable iterator + explicit prefetch opt-in. High level: (1) ResumableIterator API (language idiomatic wrappers), (2) Transport provides opaque resume_token, (3) RetryPolicy carries idempotency hint and budget, (4) default: no speculative prefetch beyond 1 page. Thoughts?
cheng: +1 to a single semantic model. Curious how we expose `resume_token` in TS/py ergonomically.
alex: concern: exposing resume tokens as opaque strings forces server-side compatibility checks. fine but document strongly. also, we need a clear migration path for current paged helpers.
maria: agreed re: migration. plan: keep old paged helpers as thin adapters over new ResumableIterator for 1 release, then deprecate.
sam: proposal for RetryPolicy: {max_retries, backoff: exponential(min, max), idempotency_hint: one_of("idempotent","non-idempotent","unknown"), budget_tokens}. The SDK can translate idempotency_hint->allowed retry types.
lia: ergonomics notes per language: Python: provide both sync iterator (.__next__) and async (async for) that expose `.resume_token` on the iterator object. TS: return an AsyncIterable whose iterator object has `resume(token)` and `peekResumeToken()` helpers. Go: return a ResumableIterator interface with `Next(ctx) (Item, error)` and `Resume(ctx, token) error`. Keep it minimal.
cheng: example TS shape (sketch):
```ts
interface ResumableAsyncIterator<T> extends AsyncIterable<T> {
  resume(token: string): Promise<void>;
  peekResumeToken(): Promise<string | null>;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```
alex: +1 on `peekResumeToken()` to avoid forcing users to materialize last page. Also: default semantics for prefetch? you said no speculative >1 page. good. we still need a built-in prefetch helper for high-latency setups (opt-in).
maria: default: prefetch window=1 (i.e., only fetch next page on iteration). provide an opt-in param `prefetch_window: number | "adaptive"` that SDK authors can enable. But default remains conservative for cost/consistency.
sam: telemetry: emit events: iterator.open, page.fetch, page.retry, iterator.resume, iterator.close. include idempotency_hint and transport used (http2/ws). ops-bot: noted: create analytics spec ticket #ANALYTICS-iter-1.
lia: transport choices: prefer HTTP/2 multiplexing for normal paged endpoints. For streaming-heavy endpoints we can enable ws/grpc-web where supported. SDK should expose a transport enum but default chosen by platform (region/compat). document fallback rules: http1->http2->ws.
cheng: retries + transport: on non-idempotent hint we should only retry safe idempotent errors (connection resets) and never retry 4xx client errors. Also, when resuming after a failure present resume_token to server side; server will validate and return 409 if incompatible. SDK should translate 409->ResumeMismatchError.
alex: implementation note: in Python async iterator we can implement prefetch as background task but cancel it on pause/close to avoid leaks. add tests to ensure no stray tasks.
maria: plan: I'll open an RFC patch with concrete interface stubs for py/ts/go, plus a migration adapter crate. Action items: alex + cheng spike sample adapter, lia write docs snippets, sam write telemetry events, ops-bot create analytics ticket. Goal: land RFC PR next week. :thumbsup:
